messages:
carmen: seeing a surge of 502/504s for hosted inference in eu-central-1a since ~09:15 UTC. Affected customers report timeouts and retries. dashboards show p95 token latency up and a spike in gateway 5xx.

raj: can you drop a couple of request IDs / trace IDs and the service hostnames so i can pull logs?

carmen: sample trace ids: trace=6a3f2c1b, trace=9c8e7a2f. hosts: infer-gw-euc1a-01/02/03. snippet from proxy logs: 
```
[09:17:32] infer-gw-euc1a-02 502 upstream reset: connection reset by peer; tcp retransmits=40; rtt=24ms
[09:18:01] infer-gw-euc1a-03 504 downstream timeout waiting for kv-cache
```

lee: ops-bot flagged increased packet loss on the crosslink between eu-central-1a <> eu-central-1b from 09:10-09:28 UTC. I've opened a ticket with transit provider (ticket #TY-5482). Provider NOC says they're seeing microburst loss on the inter-AZ fabric and are investigating. :warning:

ops-bot: alert: gateway_5xx_rate(eu-central-1a) > 8% for 5m; autofailover not triggered (policy: 10% threshold).

emily: multiple customers escalated via support — one enterprise customer reported 30% of inference requests failing, their SLA monitoring triggered and they want a postmortem + credits. Can eng confirm window and mitigation steps so we can respond?

raj: quick repro I ran from a eu-central compute node -> curl to infer-gw-euc1a shows sporadic connection resets. tcpdump on host shows bursts of packet loss during the failures. Command I used to repro: 
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sv -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":1}'; sleep 0.1; done
```

lee: i've pulled a pcap and uploaded to internal storage: https://internal.redwood/snapshots/pcap-euc1a-2819994321.pcap (restricted). Key observation: short-duration 1-2s microbursts with ~15-25% loss on specific egress paths, coincident with increased retransmits on our proxy.

raj: mitigation options — 1) temporarily shift some traffic away from euc1a to euc1b using routing policy until provider stabilizes; 2) lower autofailover threshold to trigger faster (risk: flipping during noisy periods); 3) increase transient retry window on gateway (client-facing retries) to hide blips. Recommend 1 + 3.

carmen: started traffic shift for top 20% of customer keys at 09:30 UTC (canary). rolling shift completed by 09:40. errors dropped to baseline by 09:45.

support-bot: incident note created: INC-2026-EUC1A-MICROBURST. Affected window: 09:10-09:45 UTC. Initial root cause: provider inter-AZ microbursts causing packet loss and upstream resets.

emily: thanks — i'll send customers the summary and tentative credit plan. please attach timeline & confirmation when provider gives root cause.

lee: provider update (09:58 UTC): confirmed congestion on an interconnect trunk due to scheduled maintenance side-effect + hardware queue misconfig, they applied an egress shaping fix and offered a bridge to follow up.

raj: followups: - add more granular per-az e2e tests to detect microbursts earlier - consider lowering autofailover threshold for gateway-only (not infra-wide) - add automated temp-route to shift critical tenant keys on elevated per-az 5xx alerts.

carmen: agreed on followups. i'll open a backlog ticket for the automated key-level reroute. for now incident is mitigated; keeping this thread open until provider sends final RCA. :thumbsup:
